residual.wall: Four ways to animate SVG d. Live Gasper already writes #body every frame via closedSpline. Risk is swapping the physics writer for SMIL/CSS/Flubber and breaking the 512 lock.

question: What SVG path animation techniques exist, which of them honor a locked command grammar, and which one is lawful for Gasper's #body given closedSpline + plant-gated _lp + the 25×40 cage?
coordinateSpaces: Content px. #body d is a serialization of 512 posed points, not an animation channel. Cage is 25×40. Time is the organism clock (dt), not SMIL dur.
physicalLaw: A path d is a word in a command grammar: M, C, L, Q, A, Z plus numbers. Interpolating two d strings is legal only when the command sequence is identical and corresponding numbers are the same kind (C control vs C control).
closedSpline(pts) = M p0 + N cubic Béziers (Catmull-Rom, tangent (p_{i+1}-p_{i-1})/6) + Z. N = pts.length. Live N = 512. Topology never remeshes.
Per-frame setAttribute('d', closedSpline(wpts)) is the live writer (all-script-3.js ~2923). clipBody uses the unfiltered 512. body uses wpts after _lp.
SMIL <animate attributeName='d'> interpolates matching commands. Chrome once deprecated SMIL then reversed. No springs. Fights any JS writer on the same attribute.
CSS d: path('...') and WAAPI can tween d where d is a presentation property. Safari does not interpolate d. Same-command-count still required.
JS libraries (GSAP MorphSVG, Flubber, Motion) can remesh unequal paths. That is a second topology. Forbidden for #body.
pathLength + stroke-dashoffset is a draw-on, not a shape. getPointAtLength samples an authored curve onto our lock (embedding), it does not replace the lock.
FLIP (First/Last/Invert/Play) is a layout technique for boxes. The pearl is not a box.
artisticLaw: The organism is points. d is ink. Animate the 512 / 1000, then serialize. Never animate the ink and hope the body follows.
Takes store embeddings (cage floats or 512 xy), not d keyframes. Playback = lerp points → closedSpline.
SMIL/CSS/WAAPI may dress chrome (pills, dock). They may not own #body, #clipBody, or the ribbon duals.
Stroke draw (pathLength) may reveal the grid. It may not fake a walk.
getPointAtLength is legal for snapping an authored silhouette (paddle, remote) onto the 512. Flubber remesh is not.
invariants: Do not import Flubber / MorphSVG / anime.js path morph for the hull.
512 samples. Same C-count every frame. closedSpline stays the serializer.
_lp remains the time filter. SMIL dur is not τ.
Cage 25×40 remains the shape authority. d is the rim of that embedding.
failureModes: SMIL + rAF both writing d: last-writer wins, W buzzes or pops.
CSS d tween in Safari: no interpolation, snap. In Chrome: fights _lp.
Flubber between rest and paddle: new vertex count, identity W gone.
Lerp of d strings with mismatched C counts: browser drops the animation, one-frame pop.
pathLength walk: a stroke chasing itself. Not feet.
Storing takes as d strings: yaw/LOD/closedSpline changes make old takes unloadable.
uncertainty: Safari d-as-CSS may change. Do not bet the organism on it.
Whether bloom cx/cy should stay setAttribute or move to WAAPI. Low value; leave JS.
getPointAtLength on a paddle SVG is a future embedding helper, not this cut.
tests: Painter contains function closedSpline(pts) and body.setAttribute('d',bodyD).
No <animate attributeName="d" in the live avatar markup.
No flubber / MorphSVG / anime.timeline path morph dependency for #body.
512 command count: closedSpline output has exactly pts.length C segments + Z.
visualConsequences: Walk stays socket → _lp → spline. No SMIL chew.
Morphs (paddle, puff) stay cage embeddings serialized to the same 512 C-count.
Grid reveal may use pathLength. Hull may not.
If d starts popping, someone added a second writer.
implementation: Investigate only. No painter cut this receipt.
Live writer is already the lawful one: JS rAF + closedSpline.
Next implement (if asked): take recorder stores 512/1000 floats, not d.
Optional later: getPointAtLength sampler for authored silhouettes → cage target. Not a morph library.

citations.rule: Four families: SMIL, CSS, WAAPI, JS. d morph requires same commands. CSS/WAAPI d interpolation fails Safari.
Start, end, and intermediates must have the same number of vertices in the same order or interpolation aborts.
Catmull-Rom cubics on a locked 512. d is a serialization of points already filtered by _lp.
25×40 never remeshes. Shape is an embedding. Silhouette is the rim.
